thread:
maya (PM): Rapid follow-up from today's design review: we need clearer language around guardrails and fallback behavior in the autoscale panel. Thoughts?
samir (prod-designer): Agree. Two areas: the inline banner language and the burst confirmation copy. Want to propose alternatives.
tal (frontend): Also want to lock down keyboard/screen-reader behavior for the new banner and for preset buttons. small scope change preferred.
liam (eng-run): From runtime side, we expose flags: allow_fallback, fallback_threshold, burst_enabled, burst_capacity. Need mapping to UI labels.
nana (a11y): Quick accessibility rule: any banner that changes routing must be announced (role=alert) and visible in DOM right after user action. Do not hide it behind a hover.
samir (prod-designer): Draft copy options for the banner: Option A: "This pool may not meet your latency target. Recommended: Request Dedicated. Continue will enable fallback routing to hosted variants if queues grow." Option B (short): "Latency risk detected. Request Dedicated or keep config with fallback." Which is clearer?
maya (PM): Prefer A but shorten the second sentence: keep it to one line plus actions. We should avoid jargon like "hosted variants" in the main UI.
samir (prod-designer): New phrasing: "This pool may not meet the selected latency. You can request Dedicated capacity, or keep this config and allow automatic fallback to our hosted endpoints." Too wordy?
tal (frontend): UX-wise, actions should be primary: [Request Dedicated] [Keep config]. If user picks Keep, we attach a single-line confirmation dialog: "Allow fallback routing?" with more details. That avoids surprising changes.
liam (eng-run): We need the 'allow_fallback' boolean early; the confirm dialog can set fallback_threshold too. Default threshold should be conservative (queue length > 20).
nana (a11y): Confirmation dialog must be keyboard trap and have clear focus order. Use clear labels: 'Allow fallback' vs 'Don't allow'. Avoid ambiguous verbs.
maya (PM): Good point. Samir, can you produce microcopy for the confirm dialog that is plain-language and includes billing note?
samir (prod-designer): Draft: "Allow automatic fallback routing when request queues exceed safe limits. This will route excess traffic to our hosted models to keep latency stable. Billing will apply for the served tokens as usual."
nana (a11y): Suggest replacing "as usual" with "according to your plan" — clearer. Also split into two short sentences for screen readers.
liam (eng-run): Backend will surface a short FAQ link for the dialog. We can append "Learn more" linking to docs with full behavior and thresholds.
tal (frontend): For the banner color and iconography: use an info/warning neutral tone, not red error. But ensure contrast meets AA. Also include a visible icon + text.
samir (prod-designer): Burst confirmation copy: current mock says "Approx. +$X/hr". Suggest change to "Approx. +$X/hr (varies with traffic)" to set expectation.
maya (PM): Also add a small 'Estimation basis' tooltip: "Based on your recent 5min traffic sample". Keep tooltip text short.
nana (a11y): Tooltips must not be the only source of truth. Echo the estimation basis in a small line under the cost text, visible to screen readers.
tal (frontend): Keyboard: presets on the SLO slider must be reachable via Tab. Pressing preset sets the slider and updates aria-valuetext to something like "SLO target: 200ms (Balanced)".
liam (eng-run): We'll accept both slo_ms and slo_preset in the API. Also, we'll return a 'pool_capability' object with estimated 95th ms and a boolean 'can_meet_slo'. UI can use that to show the banner.
samir (prod-designer): Microcopy for incompatible pools (when model GPU req > node GPUs): label the disabled option with short reason: "Requires 8-GPU node" and show an inline helper: "No matching nodes in this pool. Choose a different pool or request a node size upgrade."
maya (PM): If we allow advanced override, the modal must clearly state consequences: queued requests or degraded model variant. Use plain language, avoid engineering terms.
nana (a11y): Any time we show "degraded" or "queued" explain what that means for end users: e.g., "Responses may be slower or lower-fidelity."
tal (frontend): For min/max inputs, we'll keep steppers + text input. Validation message: "Max must be >= Min" in red with an icon. Also show computed "Total GPUs: N" beneath.
samir (prod-designer): Rename labels to explicit ones: "Min instances" and "Max instances" and add the microcopy: "Each instance = N GPUs". Simple.
maya (PM): Dropdown pool sort: default to "Recommended" (composite score). Add a tiny toggle in header: [Recommended ▼] and allow switching to [Cheapest] or [Most used].
tal (frontend): We'll implement as a custom combobox; ensure the header chips are operable by keyboard and announced (aria-live?) when changed.
liam (eng-run): We'll provide pool metadata: latency_score, cost_score, gpus_per_node, available_node_sizes. Frontend can render badge icons for 'Dedicated eligible' etc.
samir (prod-designer): Final copy nits: change 'ephemeral' to 'temporary' in user-facing UI. Users found 'ephemeral' confusing in tests.
maya (PM): Good catch. Use 'temporary' across microcopy. Also, add a one-line helper: "Temporary instances are billed while running." under burst info.
nana (a11y): Ensure 'temporary instances' wording is screen-reader friendly and not inside a tooltip.
deploy-bot: Preview deploy in progress: preview/autoscale-guardrail-copy -> staging. Build #8710.
tal (frontend): Will test staging for keyboard & VoiceOver and list issues here by EOD.
maya (PM): Thanks — please tag any final copy edits in Figma and we'll ship the iteration after staging pass.
